newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market ends strongly, BIL closes firmer.
newsitem.headline: NZ share market ends strongly, BIL closes firmer.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices end firmer
* BIL gains after AGM. Telecom well-bid
* TrustPower, Bay of Plenty, Infratil ease
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
319 nil * NZSC cap index +16.77 at 4,867.27
370 +5 * Volume NZ$63 million. Futures +1 at 1,179
759 +4 * Other movers - TWP.NZ -20 -15
New Zealand share prices ended on a modestly stronger note on Thursday after all but one of the top five issues edged higher.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 11.56 points higher at 2,363.40 on turnover worth NZ$66 million, much of that in the form of crossings.
Telecom was well-bid, gaining four to NZ$7.59, and Fletcher Forests looked to be recovering with a two cent gain to NZ$2.30.
"People seem to be stationing themselves around the leaders," Nigel Scott at BZW said.
Fletcher Energy had a quieter day, gaining just two to NZ$4.21, another high for the year.
BIL firmed three to NZ$1.33 following on from the annual meeting, where the company said it expected substantial improvements in Thistle hotels over the current year.
Among the smaller issues, power companies TrustPower and Bay of Plenty Electricity, along with utilities investor Infratil, all lost ground after their sharp gains on Wednesday.

Brokers said the move up and subsequent fall appeared speculative but BZW's Scott said TrustPower was "clearly in play". The market talk was for a possible merger between Bay of Plenty and TrustPower.
This would leave Power New Zealand, which has a controlling interest in Bay of Plenty, with a position in the merged group.
Infratil, with its 20 percent interest in TrustPower, was seen as a possible catalyst for the deal.
One analyst, however, noting a history of animosity between the Bay of Plenty-TrustPower camps, said such a deal did not appear likely.

However, Wednesday's movements were enough to prompt a query from the Stock Exchange, to which TrustPower replied that it was continuing to investigate acquisitions and mergers, plus other avenues of cooperation. -- James Gray (64 9 302 1253)
